In summary, our research is concerned with
the nutritional value of fruits to frugivores, and the consequences of this value on the evolution of frugivore-fruit interactions.
the role of macronutrients in determining fruit selection and seed dispersal by frugivores, and with the consequences of fruit choice for plant fitness.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the macronutritional content of the pulp of fruits from the same habitat can vary considerably.
the macronutritional content of fruit pulp does not appear to be a simple, unvarying, and unidimensional trait of fruits, at least in the Panamanian forest.
the fruit species of Barro Colorado Island are not all equal in their macronutrient composition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we found a high degree of variability in the macronutrients in the fruits of the 19 species we studied and that the differences among the species were significant and not just due to the small sample sizes we had for each species.
we have shown that fruit choice by frugivores is a complex phenomenon.
we have shown that the fruit species that are most important in terms of their contribution to the diet of the primates at Barro Colorado Island are the ones that have a high fat content.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is considerable variation among fruit species in their nutritional value, and this variation can influence fruit choice by frugivorous animals.
the macronutrients are often differentially allocated to the pulp, and this is an important factor in determining which animals are most likely to eat the fruit.
fruit macronutrient profiles vary widely across species, even when the species are found in the same forest.
